title: unable to deserialize result with property name with dashes

comments.body:
@egarim yes, this is by design. .NET 4.5 doesn't support `System.Text.Json` serialization which is the default serialization method. 

I have updated the documentation [here](https://github.com/MelbourneDeveloper/RestClient.Net/wiki/Serialization-and-Deserialization-With-ISerializationAdapter) to give more detail about this.

I recommend using Newtsonsoft serialization if you are targetting .NET 4.5 and need JSON serialization. 

Does this resolve your issue?
@egarim .NET 4.6.2 does seem to support `System.Text.Json` but RestClient.Net doesn't target 4.6.2. Do you need to use `System.Text.Json`  on 4.6.2? Couldn't you use Newtsonsoft instead?
@MelbourneDeveloper yes I can use newtonsoft instead, I was just wondering if that was an expected behavior

comments.body:
@AartBluestoke this is what the [`sendHttpRequestFunc`](https://github.com/MelbourneDeveloper/RestClient.Net/blob/6a2cbd27a6a2fca395ddb70a7659eed8db134063/src/RestClient.Net/Client.cs#L190) parameter on `Client` is for.

I'm just working on a unit test to make sure it fits your scenario.

@AartBluestoke another approach is to implement [`IRequestConverter`](https://github.com/MelbourneDeveloper/RestClient.Net/blob/main/src/RestClient.Net/IRequestConverter.cs) . This contains the method whish rensposible for converting the `Request` in to a `HttpRequestMessage`  . You can then inject implementation in to the `Client`. This is the [default one](https://github.com/MelbourneDeveloper/RestClient.Net/blob/6a2cbd27a6a2fca395ddb70a7659eed8db134063/src/RestClient.Net/DefaultRequestConverter.cs#L16).
@AartBluestoke `IRequestConverter` will be dumped in favor of a delegate in version 5.

@AartBluestoke I believe I have a solution for you. I created a branch and created a class that should manage this. Here is the [class](https://github.com/MelbourneDeveloper/RestClient.Net/blob/86a0f23516a7be54112f7560e410eecf8a8ebb2c/src/RestClient.Net.UnitTests/ManagedTokenSender.cs#L14)

Here is a [unit test](https://github.com/MelbourneDeveloper/RestClient.Net/blob/86a0f23516a7be54112f7560e410eecf8a8ebb2c/src/RestClient.Net.UnitTests/TestManagedTokenSender.cs#L28) for testing thread safety.

[This](https://github.com/MelbourneDeveloper/RestClient.Net/blob/86a0f23516a7be54112f7560e410eecf8a8ebb2c/src/RestClient.Net.UnitTests/TestManagedTokenSender.cs#L35) is where you can inject the logic for refreshing the token.

I'm keen to see if you think the unit test does actually validate the logic.

@AartBluestoke I fixed a performance issue [here](https://github.com/MelbourneDeveloper/RestClient.Net/blob/57748c6530e82c18f456794598f5207b26587d34/src/RestClient.Net.UnitTests/ManagedTokenSender.cs#L59)

Version 5 will have immutable default headers. This will mean that if you want to change the default headers, you will need to use the `With` methods for non-destructive mutation or regenerate the client. If you use IHttpClientFactory dependency injection, the `HttpClient`'s handler should not be disposed. It should be retained so there should be no performance loss.

Another approach could be to send the header on every call instead of the default headers collection.

comments.body:
@egarim actually the overload was not removed. The parameter has changed from IHttpClientFactory to a delegate called CreateHttpClient. Sorry for not communicating this well.

Here is a blog about the changes in this version:
https://christianfindlay.com/2020/06/17/restclient-net-4-0/

Importantly, this version is an attempt to allow users to inject factories with delegates instead of interfaces. Please have a read of this article: https://christianfindlay.com/2020/05/15/c-delegates-with-ioc-containers-and-dependency-injection/. It helps to decrease code while still allowing the same functionality from IHttpClientFactory. The main point is that you do not need to implement the whole interface.

All of the unit tests have been replaced with the new approach. You can still use any existing implementations of IHttpClientFactory - but they don't need to implement the interface. 

Here are some examples:

https://github.com/MelbourneDeveloper/RestClient.Net/blob/ee2f7e845b54f722e62d97250d358524946952ba/src/RestClient.Net.UnitTests/UnitTests.cs#L164

https://github.com/MelbourneDeveloper/RestClient.Net/blob/ee2f7e845b54f722e62d97250d358524946952ba/src/RestClient.Net.UnitTests/UnitTests.cs#L441

This is the most straight forward way to inject the creation of http clients in to the client:

```cs
            var client = new Client(
                baseUri: new Uri("https://restcountries.eu/rest/v2/name/australia"),
                createHttpClient: (name) => new HttpClient());
```

Please let me know if this fixes your issue.

Thanks, now my unit test are working again
